results.title: Fix: Dangerous Code Execution Function Could Allow External Attacks in scrapy/shell.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 960 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: The system shall not evaluate content originating from outside the program as executable code.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall not evaluate externally supplied content as executable code when processing shell input.

issues: The condition "when processing shell input" asserts that the evaluated content originates from input given to the shell. The evidence only locates the vulnerable call in the file scrapy/shell.py; it does not say what the evaluated content is or where it comes from.
The sentence places the condition at the end rather than following one of the EARS patterns with the condition leading, or stating the obligation unconditionally.
revision_instructions: Remove the "processing shell input" condition: the evidence identifies only the affected file, not the source or nature of the evaluated content.

Restate the remaining prohibition - that content originating outside the program must not be evaluated as executable code - in one of the EARS patterns, with any condition placed at the front of the sentence.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall not evaluate content originating from outside the program as executable code.

results.title: Fix: Unsafe Data Processing Method Allows Malicious Code Execution in scrapy/exporters.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 989 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: If previously serialised item data is read back, then the system shall process it without executing any code contained in that data.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall export data without using deserialization methods that could execute arbitrary code contained in the data.

issues: The requirement is phrased as a prohibition on a class of mechanisms ('without using deserialization methods') rather than as an observable guarantee; whether a given method is used can only be checked by reading the source, not by observing the system.

It attaches the guarantee to 'export' (serialisation) while the risk the evidence describes materialises when the serialised data is read back, so the moment at which the guarantee holds is stated imprecisely.
revision_instructions: Drop the 'without using deserialization methods' construction: state the outcome the system must guarantee rather than the category of technique it must avoid.

Tie the guarantee to the point the evidence identifies as dangerous - the processing or reading back of previously serialised item data - and express what must not happen then, namely the execution of code carried in that data.

iteration_history.candidate: If previously serialised item data is read back, then the system shall process it without executing any code contained in that data.

results.title: Fix: Unsafe XML Processing Library Could Allow Malicious Attacks in scrapy/http/request/rpc.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 852 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: When processing XML-RPC content received from an untrusted source, the system shall not execute or resolve any external entities or code embedded within that content.

iteration_history.candidate: When processing XML-RPC content, the system shall protect against malicious XML input that could compromise the application.

issues: The obligation is phrased as a protection goal rather than an observable behaviour: 'protect against malicious XML input that could compromise the application' is close to 'the system must be secure' and gives a black-box test nothing to check - no state, result or effect is named.

The qualifier 'that could compromise the application' is circular: it defines the input by the very harm the requirement is supposed to exclude, leaving more than one reasonable interpretation of what the system must do.
revision_instructions: Replace the vague 'protect against' formulation with the observable effect the evidence establishes, namely what must no longer happen when XML-RPC content originating from an untrusted source is processed.
Remove the circular qualifier 'that could compromise the application' and characterise the input independently of the harm it causes.
Keep the requirement free of any named library: the evidence only recommends one and does not state which mechanism was applied, so do not add it.

iteration_history.candidate: When processing XML-RPC content received from an untrusted source, the system shall not execute or resolve any external entities or code embedded within that content.

results.title: Ban more imports that import twisted.internet.reactor.
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 157 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent modules that import the reactor from being imported.

issues: The evidence describes a development-time restriction on the project's own source code (extending a list of banned imports, partially rolling back an earlier change), not a behaviour that the running system provides to a user or a caller.

The candidate turns this into a run-time guarantee that modules importing the reactor cannot be imported, which the evidence nowhere states; the evidence does not say what enforces the ban, when it is enforced, or which modules are affected.

Once the unsupported run-time prevention is removed, only 'some imports were banned in the codebase' remains, which establishes no observable required behaviour, so no rewrite at a higher level can be grounded in this evidence.
unsupported_claims: prevent ... from being imported (an enforcement effect at import time)
modules that import the reactor (the evidence names no set of affected modules beyond 'more imports')
the existence of a system-level guarantee rather than a codebase convention
